items.content_text:
Join us tomorrow, October 16, for Culture on 4!
 Grammy-nominated producer, songwriter, musician, and engineer Avery Johnson joins E. Foster Williams for an engaging conversation about his more than 30-year career in the music industry.
 Originally from Cleveland, Tennessee, Johnson has worked with artists including Usher, India Arie, and Outkast and is best known for producing Bone Crusher’s iconic hit “Never Scared.”
 Hear the stories behind the music, his journey from East Tennessee to international success, and insights into the creative process and music industry.
 And there’s more to enjoy throughout the evening!
 Music by DJ Mixx
 Byrd Brasi Food Truck
 Full cash bar hosted by the Bessie Smith Cultural Center
 The Smart Oasis powered by MFA pop-up shop
 📅 Friday, October 16, 2026
 🕕 6:00 PM
 📍 Bessie Smith Cultural Center | 200 E. ML King Blvd.
 🎟️ FREE and open to the public!
 Whether you’re a musician, creative professional, aspiring producer, or simply a music lover, we hope you’ll join us for an evening of music, conversation, and community.
 This special edition of Culture on 4 is presented by the City of Chattanooga’s Office of Arts, Culture and Creative Economy in partnership with Hip Hop CHA and the Bessie Smith Cultural Center.
 #CultureOn4 #Chattanooga #ChattanoogaMusic #HipHopCHA

Art has a way of telling stories that deserve to be heard. 📸
 UTC's Institute of Contemporary Art is welcoming documentary photographer Chris Aluka Berry and oral historian, writer and poet Kelly Elaine Navies to campus Nov. 5-6 for special events exploring Black Appalachian life, history and culture.
 The events accompany Berry's exhibition, “Affrilachia: Testimonies,” an eight-year photographic project documenting the people, communities and traditions of Appalachia.
 📅 Thursday, Nov. 5 | Reception at 5 p.m., followed by a public conversation at 6 p.m.
 📅 Friday, Nov. 6 | Book signing with Berry from 4:30-6:30 p.m.
 The exhibition is on display at ICA Chattanooga through Dec. 4.
 Learn more about the exhibition and upcoming events: https://blog.utc.edu/…/utcs-institute-of-contemporary-art-…/

items.content_text:
Today, Hamilton County Health Department staff wore pink and blue to recognize Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month.
 Throughout October, we honor the precious lives lost too soon, stand with families affected by pregnancy and infant loss, and remind those who are grieving that they are not alone. By raising awareness and leading with compassion, we can help break the silence surrounding pregnancy and infant loss and foster a community where every story is heard, and every life is remembered. To every family carrying these losses in their hearts, please know we see you, support you, and remember with you.

 Shortly after 3:00 p.m. Wednesday, CPD officers responded to reports of a person shot in the 1700 block of Cambridge Drive. Upon arrival, officers found a 60-year-old man with a gunshot wound. Hamilton County EMS transported the victim to the hospital where he was listed in critical condition.
 Investigators interviewed the suspect, John Billingsley, who admitted to shooting the victim. Billingsley was arrested and transported to the Hamilton County Jail and Detention Center. He is charged with Attempted 2nd Degree Murder and Aggravated Domestic Assault.
 This information is preliminary and subject to change as the investigation continues. The Chattanooga Police Department asks anyone with information regarding this incident to call 423-698-2525. 
 The charges and allegations referenced in this release are merely accusations of criminal conduct and not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt and convicted through due process of law.
 #CPDnews

 3. I believe Hamilton County is the greatest place to live, work, and play.
 After 33 years, my passion for serving and protecting this county is stronger now than ever.
 Thank you for allowing me to serve as your Sheriff. It is the honor and privilege of a lifetime.

The Health Department invites residents and families who have experienced pregnancy or infant loss, no matter how long ago, to honor their baby or babies with a personalized remembrance card.  We also invite you to join the “Global Wave of Light” on October 15 at 7 p.m. Light a candle wherever you are to remember and honor babies gone too soon, and join families around the world in a shared moment of remembrance.
 For grief resources and support, call 423-209-8051 or visit health.hamiltontn.org.

items.content_text:
The HCSO is pleased to serve as the host agency, in partnership with the @nijo.jailtraining, for the 26th annual JAILCON26 Southern Regional Conference, taking place in Hamilton County for the first time!
 With 67 agencies and 600 attendees, vendors, and instructors, this year’s event marks the largest Southern Regional Conference on record. 
 From October 13-15, the NIJO will provide law enforcement agencies with legal-based corrections training to strengthen jail operations and ensure facilities operate in accordance with legal standards. Courses include civil liability, inmate security, safety and welfare, and professional development.
 Sheriff Austin Garrett kicked off the event yesterday morning by providing a warm welcome and opening remarks.
 “As your sheriff, one of my primary objectives is to ensure our personnel are provided with the best training available to perform their duties. Partnering with The National Institute for Jail Operations to bring the 26th Annual JAILCON Regional Conference to Hamilton County helped make this specialized training available to many of our personnel and many other agencies in our tri-state region. Corrections is not just a job; it’s a highly specialized profession that requires ongoing training, critical decision-making, and a commitment to leading the way. I am proud of the incredibly challenging and professional job our corrections personnel do each day in service to our county,” stated Sheriff Austin Garrett.
 “We are here to support and educate corrections personnel. So much is misunderstood about detention, and jails are a great liability for county government. Hosting this conference in Hamilton County provides agencies across the state of Tennessee and beyond with the highest level of education. The Hamilton County Sheriff’s Office has been a great partner and advocate for the conference and legal-based training,” stated National Institute for Jail Operations Executive Director Tate McCotter.

 🪪 Voting in person? Bring an acceptable photo ID issued by the Tennessee or federal government.

Examples include voters age 60 or older, voters who will be outside their county during the early voting period and all day on Election Day, and voters unable to appear at their polling place because of hospitalization, illness, or physical disability. Other qualifying reasons apply.
 ⏰ Absentee ballot requests must be received by Saturday, October 24, 2026. Contact the Hamilton County Election Commission to confirm eligibility and request instructions.
 Completed absentee ballots must be returned by mail and received by the close of polls on November 3. A postmark alone does not meet the deadline, and hand delivery is not permitted. Request and return your ballot promptly to allow time for delivery.
 🔎 Find voting locations, hours, sample ballots, and absentee information:
 https://elect.hamiltontn.gov
 📲 Questions? Contact the Hamilton County Election Commission at (423) 209-VOTE (8683).
 Make your voting plan today!

items.content_text:
Hispanic Heritage Month is a celebration! We celebrate the richness, history, diversity, and JOY of Hispanic, Latine, and Indigenous cultures. 
 At TPUP, we create opportunities for young people to experience and celebrate culture through Dance Education; encountering history through movement, exploring traditions, and seeing their stories reflected with care and pride.
 Heritage is alive. It grows with each generation, travels with us, and continues to be shaped by those who carry it forward.
 Our ancestry grounds us.
 Education opens us.
 Movement connects us.
 And JOY reminds us there is always something worth celebrating.
 We honor where we come from.
 We celebrate who we are.
 We make space for one another to belong.
 And, siempre, we DANCE!
 Thank YOU, East Lake Elementary for inviting us to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month! 
 ¡El Mes de la Herencia Hispana es una celebración! Celebramos la riqueza, la historia, la diversidad y la ALEGRÍA de las culturas hispanas, latines e indígenas. 
 En TPUP, creamos oportunidades para que los jóvenes vivan y celebren la cultura a través de la educación en danza: acercándose a la historia mediante el movimiento, explorando tradiciones y viendo sus propias historias reflejadas con esmero y orgullo.
 La herencia está viva. Crece con cada generación, viaja con nosotros y sigue transformándose gracias a quienes la llevan adelante.
 Nuestros orígenes nos arraigan.
 La educación nos abre horizontes.
 El movimiento nos conecta.
 Y la ALEGRÍA nos recuerda que siempre hay algo que celebrar.
 Honramos de dónde venimos.
 Celebramos quiénes somos.
 Creamos espacios donde todos podamos sentirnos parte.
 Y, ¡siempre bailamos!
 ¡Gracias a Escuela Primaria East Lake por invitarnos a celebrar el Mes de la Herencia Hispana!

items.title: Congratulations to Lt. Jumaane Lanier, our Fire & Life Safety Educator, on receiving the Ralph Cothran Civil Service Fir...
items.content_text:
Congratulations to Lt. Jumaane Lanier, our Fire & Life Safety Educator, on receiving the Ralph Cothran Civil Service Firefighter of the Year Award during the 37th Annual Ruby Hurley Image Awards. The award recognizes extraordinary dedication to public safety and community service. 
 As the Public Education Officer in our Fire Prevention Bureau, Lt. Lanier holds a role that touches every corner of our city. If you want to see true passion in action, watch him talk to a room full of young students. Fire safety can easily be taught as a list of rules and warnings. But Lt. Lanier doesn't just teach rules; he connects.
 He speaks to children not just as a firefighter teaching them about safety, but as a mentor showing them what integrity, dedication, and leadership look like. He listens to their questions with patience. He encourages their curiosity. He leaves every classroom better, brighter, and safer than he found it.
 He understands that every lesson taught, every smile shared, and every seed of confidence planted in a child's mind helps build a stronger, safer community for all of us. He is following in the footsteps of his mother who was a well-known and well-respected advocate and activist in East Chattanooga. 
 By educating our children and protecting our neighborhoods, he saves lives every single day—long before an alarm ever sounds.

items.content_text:
Regional collaboration doesn't stop at state lines.

Last week, our SETD team joined leaders from Northwest Georgia, Southeast Tennessee and Northeast Alabama for Thrive Regional Partnership's 2026 Tri-State Summit.

Throughout the Summit, our team had opportunities to contribute to conversations and experiences highlighting the importance of working together across communities.

A few highlights included:

- A regional gathering of mayors from across the tri-state to discuss shared challenges and opportunities.
- Our Deputy Director Kelly Puckett moderating a panel on civic experiments and how locally driven ideas are bringing communities together.
- Our tourism coordinator participating in a paddle excursion down the Hiwassee River, sharing some insight into the Southeast Tennessee Tourism Association (SETTA), and listening to a panel explore the role tourism plays in our region's communities and economies.

These moments reflect the many ways regional collaboration takes shape, through local leadership, creative community initiatives, and the experiences that make our region unique.

We are happy to continue building a collaborative partnership with Thrive Regional Partnership and thank you for bringing together leaders and partners committed to strengthening the communities we call home

items.title: It was a busy morning for the Chattanooga Fire Department as firefighters fought back-to-back house fires.  The first fi...
items.content_text:
It was a busy morning for the Chattanooga Fire Department as firefighters fought back-to-back house fires. 
 The first fire was reported at 8:47 AM on 10/13/26 at a duplex in the 1800 block of Citico Avenue in the East Chattanooga area. First arriving units found smoke and fire coming from the back of the structure. Firefighters initiated an interior attack and took another line to the rear of the residence where flames were through the collapsed roof. Searches were conducted and no one was found inside on either side of the duplex. Fire officials learned that both sides were vacant. By 9:10 AM, the fire was out. 
 Engine 4, Engine 5, Engine 10, Squad 1, Ladder 1, Battalion 1, Battalion 3, CFD Investigations, CFD Training Division, and CFD Supply responded, along with CPD, HCEMS, and EPB. There were no injuries. 
 As crews were wrapping up operations on Citico Avenue, another house fire was reported at 9:29 AM in the 1500 block of South Highland Park Avenue off Main Street. Callers to 911 indicated that flames were visible through the front doors and windows of the home. A plume of smoke could be seen by responding companies. On the scene, crews found fire in the front of the structure. Officials quickly learned that one person was home at the time of the fire, but they made it out safely. Primary attack was made through the front door and crews continued working to extinguish the blaze. Their efforts were made difficult by the amount of contents inside the residence. By 10:01 AM, the fire was out. One adult was displaced and will be receiving assistance from the American Red Cross. The cause of the fire is under investigation. 
 Engine 1, Squad 13, Engine 9, Engine 14, Squad 1, Engine 5, Squad 20, Engine 3, Battalion 1, Battalion 2, CFD Investigations, CFD Training Division, and CFD Supply responded, along with CPD, HCEMS, and EBP. There were no injuries. 
 Fire investigators do not believe the two fires are connected in any way. Thanks to Red Shift companies for their hard work and adaptability in moving from one response to another.

Trade increasingly runs on data. 
 For goods to flow, trusted information needs to flow about how a product was made, where key inputs originated and what regulations it complies with. 
 And the demand for information is growing.
 Over the last decade, environment-related technical requirements have increased by more than 60%.
 Our new #OECD report, Better Borders for Trade, Traceability and Enforcement, shows that border systems are not keeping pace.
 Policymakers already have trade facilitation tools at their disposal to speed things up and lower costs for businesses and government:
 ➡️ Integrating new information requirements into existing streamlined systems
 ➡️ Using risk-based approaches
 ➡️ Expanding international regulatory co-operation
 Read the report to find out more: https://brnw.ch/21x6n6H

items.content_text:
Regional collaboration doesn't stop at state lines.

Last week, our SETD team joined leaders from Northwest Georgia, Southeast Tennessee and Northeast Alabama for Thrive Regional Partnership's 2026 Tri-State Summit.

Throughout the Summit, our team had opportunities to contribute to conversations and experiences highlighting the importance of working together across communities.

A few highlights included:
- A regional gathering of mayors from across the tri-state to discuss shared challenges and opportunities.
- Our Deputy Director Kelly Puckett moderating a panel on civic experiments and how locally driven ideas are bringing communities together.
- Our tourism coordinator participating in a paddle excursion down the Hiwassee River, sharing some insight into the Southeast Tennessee Tourism Association (SETTA), and listening to a panel explore the role tourism plays in our region's communities and economies.

These moments reflect the many ways regional collaboration takes shape, through local leadership, creative community initiatives, and the experiences that make our region unique.

We are happy to continue building a collaborative partnership with Thrive Regional Partnership and thank you for bringing together leaders and partners committed to strengthening the communities we call home.

We know it's spooky season, but driving shouldn't be a nightmare! The number of people driving without their lights on during recent foggy conditions has been scary. 
 Keep these safety tips in mind when driving in fog.
 1. Turn your headlights on. This not only helps you see but also allows others to see you because your taillights are on.
 2. Leave plenty of room between you and the car in front of you in case there are sudden stops.
 3. Slow down and give yourself some extra time to get where you're going. 
 Simple steps like these can help everyone reach their final destination safely.

Godsey Ridge Trails will be closed Friday, October 16 through Sunday, October 18 as we partner with Team Rubicon, a veteran-led disaster response nonprofit, for tree-felling training throughout the trail system.
 This training helps Team Rubicon volunteers prepare to respond to future storm and disaster events, while also providing an important benefit to our community through the felling of at-risk trees along the trails. By hosting this training locally, the City receives valuable trail maintenance and risk mitigation while supporting an organization that serves communities across the country when disasters strike.
 For your safety, please do not enter the trail system during the closure. The trails will reopen on Monday, October 19.
 We appreciate your patience and understanding as this work is completed.
 Learn more about Team Rubicon: https://teamrubiconusa.org/
